title: Meet Neha Thakur, 25, Himachal Pradesh’s first woman truck driver
description: It’s not easy to switch careers! But a young girl from Himachal Pradesh left her air hostess training to become a truck driver. Meet 25-year-old Neha Thakur who chose a career path few would have expected. After graduating, she worked briefly in the aviation sector and today, she spends her days behind the wheel of a 16-tonne truck, travelling across India. Neha belongs from Khudla village in Sarkaghat, Mandi district, Himachal Pradesh. She is widely known as Himachal Pradesh’s first woman truck driver. She covers her journeys in her own social-media videos and vlogs.

A Haryana native and former district-level badminton and volleyball player, Solanki joined the Indian Navy in 2012. Her journey from sports and naval service to Rashtrapati Bhavan highlights discipline, perseverance and the changing role of women in India’s armed forces.

title: Why parents keep old report cards and childhood drawings, according to psychology
description: For parents, childhood drawings and school assignments go beyond mere artifacts of nostalgia; they encapsulate rich autobiographical memories and poignant family moments. Studies reveal that nostalgic feelings can elevate the perceived value of these everyday objects. Furthermore, these keepsakes serve as visual reminders of the swift journey through parenthood, capturing the essence of time spent in care and love.

title: Atlanta man arrested after phone wipe; new ruling allows border searches

This decision follows an incident where a phone was wiped during an airport search. The ruling impacts traveler privacy and government access to electronic data. It highlights ongoing debates about digital device searches at the border.

Some view kindness as an obligation or believe they must earn affection. Likewise, receiving compliments can conflict with one's self-perception. Cultivating the ability to accept little gestures of care can significantly reduce this discomfort.
